supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Let’s fit furniture into a room.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Solve problems involving the area of ungridded figures composed of rectangles, including figures with missing side lengths.
teachingSteps: Notice the door, windows and undimensioned closet in the room plan.
Critique the furnished room and co-create mathematical area questions.
Recover room lengths and calculate the outer area and given furniture footprints.
Draw room and furniture at one scale; try non-overlapping layouts and explain access choices.
State footprint assumptions, create a poster, compare plans and complete the separate exit task.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: Do not turn an open modeling project into a single layout or unexplained 86-ft² answer. No exact closet area is given; area totals alone do not establish fit or access.

firstPartyPractice.prompt: Separate Edulytics practice: design an 8-ft by 10-ft rectangular bedroom with a 3-ft by 6-ft bed and a 3-ft by 2-ft desk. Specify door/window positions and reasonable access choices. Use a labelled scale, calculate the floor not covered by the two items, and explain your design. Teacher reviews the full plan.

independentEdulyticsCoolDown.prompt: New Edulytics exit task: an 8-ft by 10-ft rectangular room contains only a 2-ft by 5-ft bed and a 2-ft by 3-ft desk. Draw a non-overlapping arrangement inside the room, state access assumptions, and find the floor not covered by these two items. Enter the area with ft²; your teacher still reviews the plan and explanation.

stageC.humanRubric: The original three-page student PDF fixes the room’s 6-ft main width,15-ft full height,4-ft extension width and 5-ft extension height; outer area 110 ft². Bed 3×6=18 ft²; desk 3×2=6 ft². Subtracting only these non-overlapping new items gives 86 ft², explicitly before any unknown closet deduction; the original source question is not graded by that number alone. Closet dimensions are absent. Review scale, fit, rotations, no overlap, door/closet/chair access, walking routes, footprint assumptions, poster, mathematical questions and actual gallery dialogue. Many layouts can work. The source permits an own grid-paper diagram; the publisher cut-out blackline master is not claimed inspected or reproduced.

matchingScope: Only specified room spans and given footprint areas auto-check. Original layout/uncovered-floor project, closet interpretation, fit/access, poster and actual discussion remain teacher-reviewed. Distinct exit task explicitly lists all its two furniture footprints and checks64ft², still requiring design review.
